claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding suffer premature failure because of elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Introducing an Hf interlayer between zirconium-alloy cladding and an elemental Cr coating will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Reducing Cr–Zr interdiffusion with an Hf interlayer will improve Cr-coating durability in both subcritical water and accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
An Hf diffusion-barrier layer with a thickness of a few tens to approximately 100 μm is an appropriate starting intervention.
Slight interdiffusion between Hf and the zirconium alloy will form an Hf–Zr transition layer.
The resulting Hf–Zr transition layer will be controlled and stable.
The Hf–Zr transition layer will act as a diffusion barrier between the Cr coating and zirconium-alloy cladding.
The Hf interlayer will limit direct contact between Cr and Zr.
Limiting direct Cr–Zr contact will reduce the rate and extent of unfavorable Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperature.
An Hf-coated VZrHfNbTa high-entropy-alloy substrate developed an HfZr alloy transition layer through diffusion of matrix zirconium into the Hf coating during high-temperature sintering.
The Hf–Zr transition layer can enhance oxidation resistance by promoting formation of a dense protective oxide during high-temperature exposure.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the Hf-interlayer coating will have a significantly lower rate of interfacial element transport.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the Hf-interlayer coating will remain coherent across both normal-water and accident-steam thermal environments.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the Hf-interlayer coating will show reduced oxidation and improved coating integrity and service life.
The intervention is expected to function from normal reactor operating conditions in subcritical water through short steam exposures at approximately 1200–1600 °C.
The Hf interlayer may form detrimental intermetallic phases or impair bonding to the Cr coating during prolonged irradiation or corrosive exposure.
